title: Give police tasers, inquest jury urges
subtitle: Otto Vass tragedy
article: Mr. _Vass_ -- who had a history of violent outbursts when he was off his medication for manic depression and schizophrenia -- got into a fight with a group of teenagers at a 7-Eleven store at College Street and Lansdowne Avenue on Aug. 9, 2000.

A coroner's jury yesterday found that _Otto_ _Vass_ was largely responsible for the events leading up to his fatal confrontation with police six years ago, but also suggested officers be equipped with Taser guns to prevent similar deaths.

Mr. _Vass_ -- who had a history of violent outbursts when he was off his medication for manic depression and schizophrenia -- got into a fight with a group of teenagers at a 7-Eleven store at College Street and Lansdowne Avenue on Aug. 9, 2000.
Four police officers who responded to the call said they tried to arrest the man after he punched one of them in the face.
They used batons to strike his legs -- an accepted police practice -- to subdue Mr. _Vass_, who died shortly after.
It was alleged the blows caused fat to be released into the 55- year-old's blood vessels, causing a so-called "fat embolism" that quickly killed him.
The four officers were acquitted of manslaughter in 2003, but the _Vass_ family believes they used excessive force.
The inquest was called to find ways of preventing a repeat of the incident that left the father of five dead.

In its 22 recommendations yesterday, the jury said that while few psychiatric patients are violent, the "state of acute mania that Mr. _Vass_ was experiencing was a major factor in the chain of events that lead to his death."
The inquest suggested police be trained in dealing with people who are mentally ill and 911 dispatchers should tell police arriving at a scene if a suspect is making "bizarre statements."
